A public index for Singapore AI.

The Navigator is an edited starting point: useful enough to cite, open enough to correct and honest about what it does not cover.

Three domains.
Three jobs.

.com is the public index. It helps people find organizations, programmes and research without turning visibility into a paid ranking.

.org is the Commons. Organizations publish their own profiles, which appear immediately and carry a clear source status.

.ai is the Lab. It develops original questions and short field notes about how intelligence is built and used.

How we index.

Public reference

A selected starting point linked to a public source such as an official programme, institute or public research page.

Submitted

An organization has published its own profile through the Commons. It is visible immediately and has not been checked by the editor.

Claimed

The organization has contacted us to confirm that it represents the profile. Claiming confirms ownership of the page; it is not an endorsement.

Reviewed

We have checked basic public facts such as the organization name, location or homepage. Reviewed does not mean recommended or ranked.

Paid placement

Any paid enhancement is labelled on the profile and never changes its status, position in the Navigator or inclusion in an editorial note.

The Navigator is not a ranking, certification or complete census. To suggest a source, claim a profile, correct a fact or request removal, email superintelligencesg@gmail.com.

How updates work.

We update the public index when a source changes, an organization submits or corrects its own profile, or an editorial note adds a useful connection. The public record of those changes lives in the changelog.

One piece of information should be produced once and linked across the three sites: a field note can inform the index, while the organization can claim and maintain its own profile.

One initiative, three doors.
